before:
Ivory Coast's largest airport, 16 km south east of Abidjan, and the hub for Air Côte d'Ivoire. Twenty one airlines serve it across more than 30 destinations, with direct links to Europe, across Africa and into the Middle East.

Traffic is the story here. The airport carried more than a million passengers in the late 1990s, then lost much of that through a decade of political and military crisis, during which it was looted in 2004 and twice taken by French troops. With stability and economic growth it has recovered and passed its old peak, reaching 2,331,917 passengers in 2023.

It was refurbished and modernised after the unrest, and is run by Aeria, a private Ivorian company.

Access should improve again. The new Abidjan Metro, under construction since 2018, is due to serve the airport when it enters service in 2027.

It is named after Félix Houphouët-Boigny, the first president of Ivory Coast, and is also known as Port Bouët Airport.
after:
Ivory Coast's main airport lies 16 km south east of Abidjan and is the base for Air Côte d'Ivoire, the national airline. There are direct links to Europe, across Africa and into the Middle East. It handled more than 2.5 million passengers in 2025.

The airport is run under concession by the Ivorian company Aeria and has been extended and modernised.

It is named after Félix Houphouët-Boigny, a former president of Ivory Coast.

claims.note: Was '2,331,917 passengers in 2023' (the ministry's own 2023 figure, June 2025). A passenger total replaces a passenger total. claims.claim: Abidjan Metro to serve the airport from 2027
claims.wasBefore: Access should improve again. The new Abidjan Metro, under construction since 2018, is due to serve the airport when it enters service in 2027.
claims.why: No source from the last 12 months was found. The 2018 start and the 2027 target are in Wikipedia and in AIP's report of 1 February 2024 (the minister 'confident' of 2027; the 37 km line to serve seven communes including Port Bouët, without naming the airport). The ministry's 2026 budget presentation gives no date, and its rail news page reached shows nothing dated on the metro after 2023; two undated metro items in its news index (a validated model, a rail bridge at Abobo) were not read, after three attempts on this claim. A two-year-old opening date for works is not safe to repeat.

claims.claim: FCDO: e-visa before travel, collected at Abidjan airport; yellow fever certificate; Ebola screening; northern border warnings
claims.why: Held back: a warning and entry rules that replace nothing. The FCDO (updated 29 May 2026, still current 24 September 2026) says British visitors must have an e-visa approved before travel (apply at least 10 working days ahead) and collect it on arrival at Abidjan airport, must carry a yellow fever vaccination certificate, and may face Ebola health screening if arriving from affected countries. It advises against all travel within 40 km of the borders with Burkina Faso and Mali (and parts of the north) and all but essential travel within 20 km of the Liberian border; Abidjan is not in those areas. For Andy to decide whether an agent should be told.
